title: As measles outbreaks grow in the U.S., maps and charts show a record number of cases
snippet:
By mid-July, the number had already surpassed all of 2025, which had been the worst year in recent history with more than 2,200 confirmed cases. Ongoing outbreaks have put the U.S. at risk of losing its official measles elimination status, which it has held since 2000. [...] Bar chart showing the number of measles cases by year, from 2000 to present.
Total reported measles cases in 2026 (Choropleth map)

Out of the 2,289 confirmed cases last year, more than 750 were connected to an outbreak in West Texas that led to the deaths of two children.

Prior to 2025, the highest number of confirmed cases in the U.S. in recent years was 1,274 in 2019, driven by outbreaks in New York, California and Washington state. Most years the total was much lower. [...] CDC data shows about 93% of kindergartners in the U.S. were vaccinated against measles during the 2021-2022 school year and only 92.7% in the 2023-2024 school year. This is down from 95.2% during the 2019-2020 school year — a critical threshold to keep people safe. Only 10 states hit that threshold.

"When more than 95% of people in a community are vaccinated, most people are protected through community immunity (herd immunity)," the CDC states.

title: 'Not trending in the right direction': US hits record high measles cases
snippet:
July 31, 2026

The US has confirmed 2,318 measles infections already this year, surpassing the entire tally of 2025 only seven months in and reaching the highest annual total in 35 years as vaccination rates decline. Reuters Erica Stapleton takes a look at Arizona, which is among states like Texas and Virginia reporting a high rate this year.

title: US measles cases reach 35-year high, for second record-breaking year in a row | CNN
snippet:
The total number of measles cases in 2026 has already surpassed last year’s total, according to data posted by the CDC on Friday. At least 2,318 cases have been reported with more than five months left in the year. [...] Responding to measles outbreaks has become a widespread and persistent challenge in the US. Multiple outbreaks that started in 2025 continued into 2026, and new exposures have led to other large outbreaks affecting most regions of the country. [...] Measles has continued its historic resurgence in the United States this year, with a second record-breaking year in a row. Just over halfway through 2026, the country has recorded more cases than in any other year since 1991 – surpassing a grim milestone that was just topped last year.

The disease was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, but more cases have been recorded in the past 18 months than there have been in the previous 25 years combined.

title: Global Measles Outbreaks
snippet:
Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, measles cases and outbreaks continue to occur in the United States due to unvaccinated international travelers. Large measles outbreaks are possible when travel-related measles cases reach at-risk U.S. populations with low immunization against measles. In 2019, the U.S. nearly lost its elimination status with almost 1,300 measles cases from a large outbreak in New York and cases in 30 additional states. title: Map: Track the spread of measles in the U.S.
snippet:
Measles, one of the most contagious viruses in the world, is regularly infecting people in the U.S. again.

Already in 2026 more than 2,300 cases have been counted, making 2026 the two year for measles infections in the U.S. since 2000.

NBC News is continuing to track confirmed measles cases across the United States, using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data.

Measles case counts reached a 34-year high last year, and seven months into 2026, this year’s total is even higher. [...] Measles infection counts skyrocketed last year with 2,289 confirmed cases, which had been the most reported since 1991. This comes despite the virus being marked as being “eliminated” in the U.S. —a designation meaning it is no longer constantly circulating — in 2000. The U.S. is in danger of losing that status following a year of continuous spread of the disease.

Three people, including two young girls, died in the U.S. from measles last year. [...] The major outbreaks last year began with West Texas in February. In October, a measles outbreak occurred along the Utah and Arizona border. In all, the CDC recorded 48 measles outbreaks in 2025, up from 16 in 2024. So far in 2026, 35 measles outbreaks have been reported.

Childhood vaccination rates have been backsliding, leaving communities vulnerable to this deadly disease.
